subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equation of the plane which makes intercepts 1,2,4 on the x,y,z-axes respectively.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.85 — VSAQ chapter 16 The Plane, answer 103, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say where the given intercepts go, and what you do at the end.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the intercept form
steps.margin_note: First mark. This question runs the other way: the intercepts are given, so they go straight into the denominators of x/a + y/b + z/c = 1.
lines: The equation of the plane with intercepts a, b, c is  x/a + y/b + z/c = 1
∴ the required equation of the plane is  x/1 + y/2 + z/4 = 1

recall.must_convey: That the given intercepts are placed straight into x/a + y/b + z/c = 1.
accept: put the given intercepts into the denominators of the intercept form
x over a plus y over b plus z over c equals one
write the intercept form with the given numbers

steps.why: The intercept form is built to display the intercepts, so a question that supplies them needs no rearranging at all — only clearing up afterwards.
common_mistakes: Putting the intercepts in the numerators.
Assigning them to the wrong axes.

steps.label: Clear the fractions
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Put everything over a common denominator and multiply through, so the answer is in the plain ax + by + cz = d form the board expects.

recall.must_convey: That clearing the fractions gives 4x + 2y + z = 4.
accept: put over a common denominator and multiply through
clear the fractions to get the standard form
multiply everything by the common denominator

steps.why: Leaving fractions in a final answer costs marks even when the mathematics is right, so the tidy-up is part of the answer.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only some terms by the common denominator.
Leaving the answer as a sum of fractions.
